text:
mika: Quick note from today's onboarding: PTQ reranker (v4-ptq) shows reproducible NDCG variance vs fp16 on holdout-C. Suspect a mix of ANN merge nondet + quant score compression. Posting quick summary.

rahul: How big is the gap? single-run or multi-seed?

mika: Multi-seed. fp16: NDCG@10=0.459; v4-ptq: avg NDCG@10=0.436 (stdev across 4 seeds = 0.013). MRR delta ~0.018.

zara: Any evidence whether candidates differ across seeds or just reranker scores shuffle?

mika: Did a pair of controlled experiments: (1) freeze retrieval topk files and run PTQ scoring; (2) run normal retrieval + force deterministic kernels. Results: (1) variance drops to stdev 0.004, (2) variance still ~0.011. So retrieval nondet is primary driver but quant widens impact on metrics.

tom: Can you add a few sample query diffs?

mika: Example: query #q4421 "best way to parse csv with python"
- fp16 top5: [docX, docY, docZ, docW, docQ]
- ptq seedA top5: [docX, docZ, docM, docW, docY]
- ptq seedB top5: [docX, docY, docZ, docN, docW]
Scores: seedA [4.01,3.79,3.78,3.65,3.62], seedB [4.01,3.80,3.79,3.64,3.61] -> tiny deltas cause swap-ins.

infra-bot: Deterministic retrieval snapshot created: s3://redwood-eval/holdoutC/snapshots/2026-03-22/snap-1779991111

zara: We should instrument per-query topk fingerprints (concatenate id:score -> sha256) and Jaccard overlap across runs. That'll give a clear signal for CI and alerts.

rahul: Also add a per-layer ablation plan: try int8 only on early layers vs only on mid vs only tail and see which partition increases score noise most.

mika: Agreed. Proposed action items:
1) Fingerprint sweep: 5 seeds, snapshot retrieval, ptq profile, output fingerprints + per-query score stdev.
2) Layer-ablations (early/mid/tail) with deterministic retrieval to isolate scoring noise.
3) Eval harness change: default onboarding runs use snapshot retrieval + fingerprinting; alert if relative NDCG drop > 2% and mean topk Jaccard < 0.88.
4) If retrieval nondet persists at snapshot level, infra to look at ANN merge ordering.

tom: I can own a small harness patch to write fingerprints and a smoke dashboard.

zara: I'll set up an alert `rerank-ptq-topk-drift` with thresholds above and include links to run artifacts.

rahul: One more ask: record raw logits in small numeric-precision format (float16) for a sampled set of queries so we can compare kernel-level numerical differences offline.

mika: Will upload artifacts to s3://redwood-eval/holdoutC/runs/1779991111 and open a PR for harness changes. Tagging @zara @rahul @tom for reviews.

zara: Thanks — once artifacts are up Ill start the alert and run the ablation queue.
